purpose: Measure exact original browser-request cancellation event timing around release of a held real200 response. Do not change application assertions or infer product privacy acceptance.

trigger.primitive: waitCanceled requestfailed waiter at driver258, before heldActualGET.release at552
trigger.qualification: Original request exact event was not observed within that waiter. Current /auth/me403 is not identified as the timed-out primitive. No application bug or lifecycle cause is proven by this alone.

runtime.package_reuse: Identical accepted download/version/integrity/member extraction guards; no npm install/new dependency. Hosted download absolute90s/max20MiB,90MiB unpacked/6000members.

synthetic_only.source: Node built-in http, static literal HTML/native XHR+AbortController only; no React/app/DB/auth/private data/fixtures.
synthetic_only.data: One fixed synthetic old-value sentinel, never printed. No real identifiers/contact/body/cookies/headers/URLs/errors in result records.
synthetic_only.network: Container networknone; browser only two exact loopback origins/paths allowed; all other routed requests abort/count; expected external0.
synthetic_only.credentials: Runtime env-i only fixed PATH/HOME/CI/browser location/Node memory. No credentials/app/env file/source mounts.

sequence.each_case: New context/page; real browser XHR routed and originalRequest identity captured; route.fetch actual200 with maxRetries0/maxRedirects0/timeout15s; original route remains paused at a gate. Listeners for exact original context/page requestfailed/requestfinished/response are armed before request.
sequence.actions: Abort case user clicks native AbortController button which calls real XHR.abort via actual signal; reload uses page.reload; close uses page.close then opens a fresh static page. No route.abort is used to manufacture target-request cancellation.
sequence.ordering: Start lifecycle action, observe exact events up to1s while original route remains held, snapshot booleans/counts/action-settled state, then release the same real200 once and await handler disposal/cleanup. Observe terminal events up to2s after release plus live-document protocol roundtrip. Never assume failure event exists in either window.
sequence.fulfill: If actual original.failure exists, record not_attempted_failed; otherwise call route.fulfill with the exact actual response. Finite returned/target_closed/other_error outcomes are observations, not proof that response reached browser.
sequence.retirement: Abort action requires actual native onabort observation and no oldvalue rendered. Reload/close require a different server document generation, oldpage closed onlyclose, freshpage onlyclose, no stalevalue in live replacement. No private UI implementation exists in this synthetic probe.
sequence.total: Exactly3 real server data fetches/3 contexts closed, browser and2servers closed; no screenshots/artifacts.

record_contract.limits: Each record<=1024B; wholeprivate log<=32768B; exact keys/types, unique ordered3cases, exact finite OBSERVED result, bounded integers, no arbitrary messages.
record_contract.observations: before/after exact context/page failed event counts0..1, actual request.failure Boolean, finished counts0..1, original browser response status null|200, finite fulfill return outcome, handler/disposal booleans, actual nativeabort Boolean|null, action completion before release, oldpage closure/document retirement/newpage/stalevalue flags, measured observation elapsedms.
record_contract.acceptance: Only structural observation completion with all3 genuine actions/source-controlled cleanup and process0/stopped/nonOOM. FAILURE always prevents completion even with later RESULT. No test requires cancellation true/false or invents canceled states. Product_acceptance permanentlyfalse.

cleanup: Unique run+nonce ownership label; validate container ownership/networknone before start; inspect typed actual client/native/Running/OOM before stop; stop if necessary; EXITtrap removes only matching owned containers and proves absence, validates/removes owned scratch. Pinned shared image is pulled, not rebuilt/tagged/deleted; no image ownership claimed.

APIRequestContext fetch and separate route fulfillment.
requestfailed originates loadingFailed; already-canceled protocol interception can be tolerated.
